name: Easy One-Pot Black-Eyed Pea Stew With Swiss Chard and Dill

ingredients.name: extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for drizzling
finely chopped fennel, from 1 large bulb
freshly ground black pepper, plus more for serving
chopped fresh dill, plus more for serving
fresh lemon juice, from 1 medium lemon

instructions.primary_message: In a large pot, heat oil over medium-high heat until shimmering. Add onion, fennel, carrot, and 1 teaspoon kosher salt. Cook, stirring occasionally, until vegetables soften, 7 to10 minutes.

Stir in garlic, paprika, cumin, and black pepper, and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute. Add diced tomatoes, and cook, stirring constantly and scraping up any browned bits on bottom of skillet, until tomatoes start to simmer, 2 to 3 minutes.

Stir in black-eyed peas, broth, and remaining 1 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat. Reduce heat to a simmer, and cook, stirring occasionally, until flavors meld and mixture slightly thickens, 8 to 10 minutes. Add Swiss chard and cook until it turns bright green, about 2 minutes. Remove from heat and then stir in dill and lemon juice.
Divide stew evenly among 4 bowls. Top each bowl with 1 tablespoon yogurt and sprinkle evenly with dill, black pepper, and olive oil. Serve.

description: This one-pot black-eyed pea stew is brothy, filling, and made with Swiss chard, dill, lemon, and pantry staples.
notes: Make-ahead and storage: Leftovers can be refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 4 days.
author: Laila Ibrahim
